analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md. The PR is documentation-only: a date bump on line 3 and a new passage after base line 955 (head 956-986) about an excluded startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The patch excerpt is truncated, so the final head lines were not visible.

Security-relevant claims in the visible text:
- The warmup trains no rates or counters and is bounded by a 20-second wall budget.
- It uses a greedy 128-token probe, run twice, to detect a cold compile cache.
- It uses the artifact's default sampling for the solo prompt and the served-width cell.
- It runs after self-test and before registration, so routed traffic cannot preempt it.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-041 / A-001: the warmup prompts are synthetic, so they do not introduce consumer data. If the warmup uses an SSD prefix cache or cacheSalt, that was not visible. A warmup that donated a synthetic prefix would be low-impact. Prefix-cache identity and scoping could not be verified from the docs alone.
- T-029 / T-016 and other availability concerns: the 20 s budget and the once-per-engine rule bound the cost.
- TB-011: warmup before registration does not alter authorization. No gating or attestation change is described.

No code changes are in scope, so no regression was identified. Open questions for integration:
- whether the warmup implementation really bypasses the SSD prefix-cache donation path;
- whether warmup runs before registration without delaying App Attest challenge handling, since the doc says suspended work must not delay it.
These rest on the implementation, which was not supplied, and the truncated patch tail was not seen, so I set needs_deeper_review false only for the documentation scope.
